body:
A failed `Sudo.sudo` can report success through the blocking SDK. `Sudid` decodes to `{sudo_result: Err(...)}`, but the current client looks for `result` and then tests the entire attribute map for `Err`. Outer `System.ExtrinsicSuccess` therefore hides the inner failure.

Add ungated `protocol::receipt` and use it in the blocking client. It resolves all six Python-supported nested-result events, including `SudoAsDone`, `Utility.BatchInterrupted` and `Utility.ItemFailed`; retains the five MevShield failure forms; and uses the last `TransactionFeePaid.actual_fee`, falling back to checked Treasury/Balances deposit sums. Native fee amounts must fit `u64` rao. Existing `TxOutcome` field types and semantic-code conversion remain intact.

The regression encodes `Sudid(Err(BadOrigin))` and outer success through actual Finney v478 V15 `System.Events` metadata, then decodes it with the public storage helper. The resulting attributes contain `sudo_result` and no `result`; the new resolver returns failure. The resolver rejects missing required fee, weight, and outer failure attributes; nested wrapper discovery follows Python and skips absent result fields. Live Sudo-wrapper evidence from the later integration scenario is still pending.

This depends on #3246's portable protocol helpers and #3243's value navigation. The diff includes those commits until they merge; the receipt-specific commit follows them.

Rust 1.89 validation: four portable receipt regressions, 26 inherited portable helper tests, and 71 all-feature library tests pass (one existing test requiring physical OpenCL GPUs ignored). All-feature/all-target core and binding Clippy, the portable wasm check and formatting pass. PyO3 checks use `PYO3_NO_PYTHON=1`; Python tests remain in CI.
title: sdk: detect Sudo and other nested receipt failures
